mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate environment reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5 percentage points within three months signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month moving average) fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%), labor market weakness suppresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity and economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter).
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% indicates a strengthening housing market and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary easing cycles (FEDFUNDS declining), the central bank's accommodative policy boosts liquidity and risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a labor market mismatch where job creation is outpacing labor force participation, signaling economic fragility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS growth > 0.2% and UNRATE rising > 0.1pp) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases.
